exposure: Risk factors for hyperglycemia in pregnancy (HIP): body mass index >=25 kg/m2, age >= 35 years, family history of diabetes, personal history of HIP or macrosomic infant
outcome: Composite endpoint: preeclampsia, large-for-gestational-age infant, shoulder dystocia
cohort: 4518 women with no known diabetes who underwent complete universal screening for HIP at the study department between 2012 and 2016.
finding: Risk factors for HIP were predictive of both HIP diagnosis and a composite endpoint of HIP-related events, regardless of actual HIP status, suggesting that modifiable risk factors like overweight/obesity could be targets for improving pregnancy outcomes.
